summary: The [digital economy master plan for 2024 to 2034](2024-01-01 Gambia National Digital Economy Master Plan 2024-2034) is the framing instrument, with no mid-term review or costed implementation plan held.
developments:
A ten-year science, technology and innovation policy for 2027-2035 was validated, after its minister conceded the previous one achieved none of its objectives ([validation](2026-08-31-thepoint-gambia-sti-policy-2027-2035-validation)).

It was adopted for a ten-year period and its position is unchanged ([master plan](2024-01-01 Gambia National Digital Economy Master Plan 2024-2034)).

No monitoring report, budget allocation against it or delivery milestone appears anywhere in the base, and no domestic budget appropriation for the digital sector is held at any date, so a ten-year plan runs without a measurable financing line behind it.

summary: The [national data policy](2025-01-01 National Data Policy 2025 - The Gambia (draft)) has been a published draft since 2025 with no adoption, gazetting or implementing instrument.
developments:
It was published by the communications ministry as a draft and has not moved ([draft policy](2025-01-01 National Data Policy 2025 - The Gambia (draft))).

It sits beside an enacted data-protection statute and a validated interoperability architecture, so the policy layer is the one part of the data stack that has stalled rather than the whole of it.

summary: The [digital identity strategy for 2023 to 2028](2024-05-17 Validation of The Gambia's National Digital ID and Digital Transformation Strategy) is in force and now carries a delivered system, with no statute governing it.
developments:
The strategy was validated at a supported workshop in May 2024 and provided for a system that has since been built ([validation](2024-05-17 Validation of The Gambia's National Digital ID and Digital Transformation Strategy), [strategy](2024-01-01 Gambia National Digital Identity Strategy (Strategy Report))).

What the base does not hold is the legal basis for issuing identity cards outside the country, which the opposition alleged was unlawful in August 2025 for issuance in Mauritania, Congo and Togo; no official response, regulation or registry statement has followed ([allegation](2025-08-11-udp-alarm-unlawful-id-cards-abroad-thepoint)).

summary: The [Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act 2025](2025-12-26 Review of Gambia's Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2025) was enacted after several stalled years, with extraterritorial scope and seven lawful bases.
developments:
It carries a sensitive-data regime covering genetic, biometric and health data, and rights of access, rectification, erasure and protection from solely automated decisions ([review](2025-12-26 Review of Gambia's Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2025)).

Passage was in October 2025 ([passage](2025-10-13 Gambia Passes Landmark Data Protection and Privacy Law)).

No implementing regulation, commencement notice or first enforcement action under it is held, and the commission that would supervise it is not separately constituted on the record.

summary: The [Information Commission](2026-08-17-gambia-information-commission-communication-strategy) carries both the access and the data-protection statutes, and is receiving donor support to raise awareness of them.
developments:
The support is funded under a peacebuilding project to build a communication strategy raising public awareness of the two Acts ([support](2026-08-17-gambia-information-commission-communication-strategy)).

No budget, staffing, caseload or enforcement record for the commission is held, and awareness-raising support is not evidence of enforcement capacity. It is one body carrying two statutes, one of them enacted only in 2025.

summary: The Act is in force but [most public institutions have yet to appoint the information officers it requires](2026-08-07-gambia-gpu-access-to-information-implementation), and requests go unanswered.
developments:
Twenty-one-day statutory requests are going unanswered, on the press union's account of 7 August 2026 ([union account](2026-08-07-gambia-gpu-access-to-information-implementation)).

No government response, compliance count or enforcement action is on record, so a statute that exists is being reported as unimplemented by the constituency that uses it, and by nobody else.

summary: The [Communications Bill 2025](2026-03-03-lawmakers-back-communications-bill-2025-standard) passed second reading in March 2026 and covers electronic commerce, signatures and cybercrime in one instrument.
developments:
It also covers electronic communications and broadcasting, and was referred to National Assembly committees after the second reading on 2 March 2026 ([second reading](2026-03-03-lawmakers-back-communications-bill-2025-standard)).

The press union is pressing for repeal of the restrictive media laws around it ([committee stage](2026-07-22-thepoint-lawmakers-engaged-communication-bill)).

No enactment date is held, and until it passes the country has no electronic transactions or electronic signature statute at all.

summary: A [State Intelligence Service Bill](2026-07-31-sis-validates-bill-to-reposition-as-robust-futuristic-intelligence-service) validated in July 2026 is reported to require judicial warrants and oversight for intrusive measures.
developments:
It would also give the National Assembly review of the Service's budgets and operations; it has not been tabled ([validation](2026-07-31-sis-validates-bill-to-reposition-as-robust-futuristic-intelligence-service)).

The text is not held and the Bill does not appear in the Assembly's bills library, so the provisions are as reported from a workshop. It is the only instrument in the base that would put a limit on state access to personal data, and it exists as an account of a draft.

summary: [Draft broadcasting and online content regulations](2026-04-02-pura-gambia-draft-broadcasting-and-online-content-regulations-2026) went out for consultation in April 2026, one of seven instruments released together.
developments:
The draft is made under section 226(1) of the Information and Communications Act in consultation with the regulator; its fourteen parts run from general obligations through a content complaints committee, licensing and professional standards, classification tiers, content monitoring, local content, public service broadcasting, watershed and children's programming, and enforcement ([draft regulations](2026-04-02-pura-gambia-draft-broadcasting-and-online-content-regulations-2026)).

The information minister set out its child-protection provisions in August 2026, covering the identity of child victims, parental consent for interviews with children, and content that harms or exploits minors ([provisions](2026-08-16-voice-gambia-le-ministre-de-l-information-exhorte)).

Its execution block is unsigned and undated, and no consultation closing date or adoption date is published. The seven instruments include journalists registration guidelines, which is the part the press constituency is contesting.

summary: The revenue authority [convened the continental tax forum's master class](2026-07-23-gambia-gra-banjul-hosts-ataf-commissioners-general-master-class) at Banjul in July 2026.
developments:
The forum's executive secretary argued there that digital systems deliver only alongside governance reform, and pressed for a united African position in the United Nations tax convention negotiations ([master class](2026-07-23-gambia-gra-banjul-hosts-ataf-commissioners-general-master-class), [proceedings](2026-07-23-gambia-africas-tax-chiefs-confront-threat-to-national-revenues)).

It is the country's only convening role in the base, and the argument made at it, that digitisation without governance reform does not raise revenue, is the sharpest external check on the tax-digitisation claims recorded elsewhere on this ledger.

The bilateral digital-cooperation memorandum signed at Dakar on 12 June 2026 held its first steering-committee session at Banjul on 29 August 2026, settling four priorities — infrastructure and interoperability, cyber resilience, capacity building and regulatory harmonisation — with rural electronic-government access named among the work ([steering committee](2026-08-29-senegal-gambie-feuille-route-numerique-commune)).

No timetable, budget or named deliverable is attached to any of the four priorities, so what the committee has agreed is a list of headings.

summary: A [regulatory cooperation and free-roaming agreement with Senegal](2026-06-26-senegal-gambia-digital-integration-regulatory-cooperation-techreviewafrica) was signed in June 2026, adding to a three-country roaming memorandum of 2025.
developments:
The Senegal agreement covers telecommunications regulatory cooperation and free roaming, with no commencement date or tariff published ([agreement](2026-06-26-senegal-gambia-digital-integration-regulatory-cooperation-techreviewafrica)).

A roaming memorandum with Liberia and Sierra Leone signed in February 2025 is unchanged, with no tariff, traffic or commencement figure published ([memorandum](2025-02-05-west-african-roaming-mou-lbr-gmb-sle)).

Two roaming instruments in eighteen months and no traffic or price figure for either is the position: the agreements are signed and their effect is unmeasured.

summary: A [three-month customs roadmap with Senegal](2026-07-20-thepoint-gra-senegal-customs-ict-transit) was agreed in July 2026 to exchange customs data by interface across three border posts.
developments:
The roadmap installs a shared customs system at Karang, Keur Ayib and Selety within three months, deploys transit tracking, exchanges customs data by interface once the system is live, replaces transit agents with a single administrative document and reactivates an intelligence platform ([roadmap](2026-07-20-thepoint-gra-senegal-customs-ict-transit)).

It is the only cross-border data-sharing arrangement in the base, and no data-protection provision, retention rule or custodian is stated for the customs data it would exchange.

summary: A [national enterprise architecture](2026-05-22-gambia-validates-national-enterprise-architecture-govstack-techreviewafrica) was validated in May 2026 as the interoperability blueprint, and is not adopted, funded or implemented.
developments:
It was validated under an international open-standards initiative ([validation](2026-05-22-gambia-validates-national-enterprise-architecture-govstack-techreviewafrica)).

A blueprint validated and not adopted is the same position the data policy is in, and both sit behind an identity system and a data centre that are already running, so the standards layer is arriving after the systems it would govern.

summary: Tax collection [rose to D25bn in 2025 from D11bn in 2022](2026-07-30-gambia-digital-reform-doubles-tax-revenue-d25b), which the finance minister attributes to digitalisation of collection.
developments:
The tax-to-gross-domestic-product ratio rose from 9 per cent in 2022 to 13 per cent in 2025, stated by the minister at the Banjul master class ([ratio](2026-07-23-gambia-gra-banjul-hosts-ataf-commissioners-general-master-class)).

The authority's 2026 target is D27.5bn ([target](2026-08-03-gambie-numerisation-recettes-fiscales)).

The attribution to digitalisation rather than to rate increases is the minister's own and is an attribution, not an evaluation; no counterfactual, rate schedule or compliance analysis is published beside it. No domestic appropriation for the digital sector is held at any date.

summary: The [US$50m regional digital grant](2023-11-07-worldbank-dtfa-wardip-sop1-pad4756) is in implementation with no disbursement or results figure published in three years.
developments:
It is SDR 38.1m, stated as US$50.0m equivalent at approval in November 2023, inside a US$293m regional operation with three neighbouring states and three continental bodies ([approval](2023-11-07-worldbank-dtfa-wardip-sop1-pad4756), [operation](2023-01-01-world-bank-gmb-2023-wardip-sop1-gambia-bw01)).

A second operation, about US$1m covering this country and Sierra Leone jointly, remains a pipeline entry with no approval, signature or first disbursement held ([pipeline](2025-01-01-afdb-gmb-002-gambia---digital-innovation-for-government)).

A third, about US$3m to pilot a payment system aligned to an open standard, is recorded closed with no evaluation or successor held ([closed pilot](2024-01-01-gates-gmb-001-the-gambia-digital-for-development)).

summary: An [80 per cent stake in the mobile incumbent was transferred](2026-07-10-gamtel-ycell-share-investment-modernization-thepoint) in July 2026 against a GMD 6.1bn modernisation programme.
developments:
The programme covers fourth- and fifth-generation radio access, core, operations and billing systems, hybrid tower power and revenue assurance ([agreement](2026-07-10-gamtel-ycell-share-investment-modernization-thepoint)).

The announced winning bid was D6.7bn and the signed commitment GMD 6.1bn, and the base does not reconcile the two ([bid](2025-12-11-govt-sell-80pc-gamcel-d6bn-ycell-standard)).

Separately a US$50m partnership was signed in January 2026 to take the national backbone from 40 Gbps to 800 Gbps, with no completion date, milestone schedule or local-currency figure published ([partnership](2026-01-05-gamtel-sysroad-50m-ppp-broadband-techafricanews)).

summary: A [US$50m partnership](2026-01-05-gamtel-sysroad-50m-ppp-broadband-techafricanews) signed in January 2026 would take the backbone from 40 Gbps to 800 Gbps, on a network still carrying a 2017 concessional loan.
developments:
No completion date or milestone schedule is published for the upgrade ([partnership](2026-01-05-gamtel-sysroad-50m-ppp-broadband-techafricanews)).

The existing network was built under a US$25.9m concessional loan repayable by the state operator, with a servicing history of arrears cleared in June 2020 and the loan collateralised against a minimum escrow balance accessible to the lender ([loan](2017-12-22-eximbank-cn-gmb-001-record)); no statement of network condition, utilisation or debt position has followed since ([loan](2017-12-22-eximbank-cn-gmb-001-record)).

summary: The mobile incumbent's [network modernisation is contracted](2026-07-10-gamtel-ycell-share-investment-modernization-thepoint) at GMD 6.1bn, covering fourth- and fifth-generation radio access and core systems.
developments:
The agreement was signed on 9 July 2026 alongside the equity transfer ([modernisation](2026-07-10-gamtel-ycell-share-investment-modernization-thepoint)).

No subscription series, penetration rate, coverage figure or market-share statistic is published by the regulator at any date, so a contracted upgrade is the only forward-looking connectivity evidence the base holds and there is nothing to measure it against.

summary: A satellite licence remains [withheld after more than a year](2026-05-24-gambia-starlink-licence-delayed), the minister stating the applicant needs a general satellite licence rather than the permit sought.
developments:
He stated on 24 May 2026 that he had refused to approve the permit and that the applicant lacks the competencies and equipment for the terminal permit ([refusal](2026-05-24-gambia-starlink-licence-delayed)).

A fee was paid and the licence left unissued for over a year, the government citing due diligence in the face of United States pressure ([due diligence](2025-07-10-govt-due-diligence-us-pressure-starlink-standard)), and the delay has been argued in public as a transparency and trust question ([public argument](2026-03-03-starlink-gambia-transparency-trust-delay-standard)).

The base carries a fee paid in December 2024 and a permit payment in February 2026, and whether these are the same payment is not established.

summary: A [national data centre](2026-07-01-barrow-inaugurates-national-data-centre-nims-standard) was inaugurated in July 2026 and hosts the national identity management system.
developments:
It was opened alongside the identity system itself on 1 July 2026 ([inauguration](2026-07-01-barrow-inaugurates-national-data-centre-nims-standard)).

No capacity, tier rating or operating cost is published, so the state's own hosting position is established by an opening ceremony and by the one system known to run in it.

summary: The [first private data centre](2026-04-30-barrow-qgroup-house-first-data-centre-thepoint) entered service in April 2026, on a base that had held no data centre of any kind.
developments:
It was built by a domestic group with a mobile operator and a long-term foreign vendor ([inauguration](2026-04-30-barrow-qgroup-house-first-data-centre-thepoint)).

With the state facility opened three months later, the country went from no data centre to two in a single quarter, and no capacity, occupancy or price figure is published for either.

progress: No change, a first measurement with nothing tying it to the digital estate
summary: [23 MWp of solar with 8 MWh of storage](2025-02-10-renewables-boost-sustainable-development-car-gambia) entered service in February 2025, one of two parks under a combined US$149m investment.
developments:
The two parks total 48 MWp and are stated to provide new or improved electricity to 500,000 people across two countries ([solar parks](2025-02-10-renewables-boost-sustainable-development-car-gambia)).

The beneficiary figure is the two countries combined with no national count stated, and no source ties the generation to the digital estate. No power supply position for the national digital systems is held at any date, against two data centres opened in 2026.

summary: The [cybersecurity strategy for 2022 to 2026](2022-09-01-gambia-national-cybersecurity-strategy-action-plan-2022-2026-revised) runs out at the end of this year, with no successor, mid-term review or implementation report held.
developments:
Its four pillars are legal and regulatory strengthening, identification of critical information infrastructure, child online safety, and compliance with international standards and treaties, and its training and awareness uptake target was dated by 2023 ([strategy](2022-09-01-gambia-national-cybersecurity-strategy-action-plan-2022-2026-revised)).

The same document is the only source for the country's incident-response arrangements, and it describes an institutional design rather than a capability: a national response team operating a cybersecurity centre with a security operations centre inside it, a coordination directorate, a commission, an advisory board, sectoral focal points, sector response teams and a police cybercrime unit.

Nothing held states that any of those bodies is standing, and no incident report, budget line or annual report naming any of them exists.

summary: A [national identity system went live](2026-07-03-gambia-launches-sovereign-digital-id-margins-biometricupdate) in July 2026 and nationwide rollout of ten-year biometric cards began on 7 August at six centres.
developments:
Field reporting from biometric identity enrolment centres in the Greater Banjul Area found high demand meeting daily processing caps ([reporting](2026-08-28-foroyaa-gambians-welcome-biometric-id-rollout)). The base holds no enrolment total.

The system issues instant cards from the national data centre, and the cards are produced with a Ghana-based supplier; no enrolment or issuance figure has been published since launch ([rollout](2026-08-07-gambia-national-identity-cards-rollout), [launch](2026-07-03-gambia-launches-sovereign-digital-id-margins-biometricupdate)).

It runs under an eight-year design-build-finance-operate-transfer contract signed in January 2026, with a 70/30 revenue share, ten-year card validity, free replacement of valid cards and a second-phase data centre; no contract value is published in anything held ([contract](2026-01-21-govt-signs-id-card-deal-margins-thepoint), [terms](2026-01-27-new-id-card-10-years-validity-standard)).

The arrangement it replaced was a foreign concession the government had resolved to end, so the country moved from a concession to a build-operate-transfer contract rather than to direct state issuance.

summary: The [electronic civil registration system](2024-03-28 A Transformative Journey of Mass Birth Registration and Health Insurance in The Gambia) holds about 1.17m people with a unique identification number, and its integration with the identity card has produced no milestone.
developments:
A mass birth-registration and health-insurance campaign reached about 1.17m people, and the system is described as the interoperability backbone ([campaign](2024-03-28 A Transformative Journey of Mass Birth Registration and Health Insurance in The Gambia)).

A June 2025 commitment to integrate it with identity cards and the passport has produced no published integration milestone in the fourteen months since ([commitment](2025-06-20-govt-integrate-id-cards-ecrvs-thepoint)).

That matters more now than it did: an identity system went live in July 2026 and the register that would feed it is on the same unchanged footing it held two years ago.

summary: The [social registry](2024-04-23 The Gambia Social Registry - A Success Story in Systems Building) holds 203,022 households across 40 of 43 districts, about 70 per cent of the population, with no coverage update since.
developments:
It was built in two years and carries the national cash transfers ([registry](2024-04-23 The Gambia Social Registry - A Success Story in Systems Building)).

Its coverage is cited internationally as a systems-building success ([global comparison](2025-07-15 Global Insights on Social Registries - Coverage and Beyond (World Bank))).

No update has been published since 2024, so a register described as near-complete is measured at a point two years old, and its relationship to the identity system launched in 2026 is not stated anywhere.

summary: The [first unified national land policy](2026-08-12-gambia-national-land-policy-2026-2035) mandates a digitalised land administration system and a centralised land information system.
developments:
The policy for 2026 to 2035, published in August 2026, also requires digitised land registration alongside new certificates of customary ownership, backed by a costed ten-year implementation roadmap ([policy](2026-08-12-gambia-national-land-policy-2026-2035)).

It is a policy mandate rather than a build: no supplier, budget line, custodian or start date for either system is stated, and no data-protection provision for the land record is reported despite a data-protection statute enacted the year before.

summary: [212,095 supplementary registrations were announced against 179,445 records](2026-08-07-gambia-iec-voter-register-discrepancies) on the data given to parties, with 1,600 objections filed.
developments:
The commission attributes the gap to unverified processing outputs; the discrepancy was raised by opposition parties at a stakeholder forum ahead of the December 2026 presidential election, and no reconciled figure has been published ([discrepancy](2026-08-07-gambia-iec-voter-register-discrepancies)).

The objections, on eligibility and residency, are being heard by revising court magistrates before the provisional register merges with the 2021 register; the chairman states the register will be credible once the court finishes, that the names removed were multiple registrations covered by an earlier amnesty, and that no eligible registrant has been omitted ([assurance](2026-08-18-point-iec-chair-assures-gambians-credible-voter), [objections](2026-08-07-gambia-iec-1600-objections-voter-registration)).

Partial digitalisation of the December polls was announced in March 2026, covering polling-station mapping, results transmission and tablets, with no procurement, test or audit arrangement published ([digitalisation](2026-03-12 Gambia IEC introduces partial digitalisation ahead December polls)).

summary: A [national digital addressing steering committee](2025-10-13-gambia-launch-ndasc-digital-nation-techafricanews) was launched in October 2025, on a policy dating from 2023.
developments:
No national coverage figure or rollout milestone has been published since ([committee](2025-10-13-gambia-launch-ndasc-digital-nation-techafricanews)).

The only measured addressing anywhere in the base is municipal, which makes a national committee launched two years after its own policy the weaker half of the record.

summary: One municipality has [georeferenced 36,000 properties](2025-12-01 Implementing a Comprehensive Digital Addressing System - Kanifing Municipality, The Gambia), feeding property-tax billing and waste management.
developments:
The addressing system uses open location codes and is the only working subnational record system in the base ([municipal addressing](2025-12-01 Implementing a Comprehensive Digital Addressing System - Kanifing Municipality, The Gambia)).

No revenue figure, billing coverage or comparison with the pre-digital position is published, and no other local authority appears anywhere in the record.

summary: A [digital single-window business registration system](2026-08-04-trans-gambia-economic-zone-set-to-create-3400-jobs-as-investor-interest-grows) is being finalised, with more than 350 agricultural enterprises digitally mapped.
developments:
The trade minister stated on 4 August 2026 that the system is being finalised, inside a programme reaching more than 4,050 firms ([registration system](2026-08-04-trans-gambia-economic-zone-set-to-create-3400-jobs-as-investor-interest-grows)); no launch date is published ([registration system](2026-08-04-trans-gambia-economic-zone-set-to-create-3400-jobs-as-investor-interest-grows)).

The mapped enterprises are a sector programme's output rather than the register's, so what exists is a mapping exercise and a system said to be near completion.

summary: An [instant payment system](2025-12-15 Gambia launches BANTABA 2.0, first real-time interoperable payment system) launched in December 2025 across banks, mobile money, microfinance and fintechs.
developments:
It is built on an open-source core and operated by the national switch; no transaction volume has been published ([launch](2025-12-15 Gambia launches BANTABA 2.0, first real-time interoperable payment system)).

A partnership signed in June 2025 to take public transport fares by mobile money is unchanged, with no deployment, route or volume figure published in the fourteen months since ([transport fares](2025-06-20-wave-gambia-gtsc-digital-payment-partnership-thepoint)).

summary: A [wallet was authorised to collect all government-service payments](2026-03-02 Gambia Gov't payments now digitalised live on Yonna Wallet app) in March 2026, and a second platform was wired into revenue collection in July.
developments:
The first collects identity card, passport and business-registration fees with diaspora payment and auto-generated receipts; no volume or fee structure is published ([authorisation](2026-03-02 Gambia Gov't payments now digitalised live on Yonna Wallet app)).

A memorandum with the Accountant General wires a domestically built platform, distributed through the postal service, into government revenue collection, with no go-live date, volume, fee structure or list of connected banks published and no text of the memorandum held ([memorandum](2026-07-20-gambia-accountant-general-sutura-digital-revenue-collection)).

Two collection channels authorised in five months, neither with a published volume, is the position.

summary: A [blockchain payment-distribution pilot](2026-08-06-biometricupdate-undp-blockchain-dpi-pilots-deployment) is running with a United Nations agency, grouped with pilots in four other countries.
developments:
The agency reports distribution costs cut from about 10 per cent to as little as 2 per cent across the five pilots, an aggregate figure not disaggregated for this country ([pilots](2026-08-06-biometricupdate-undp-blockchain-dpi-pilots-deployment)).

No country-specific volume, beneficiary count or launch date is published, and the agency names governance, interoperability and trust as the remaining barriers before country-programme integration.

summary: [Individual learner tracking and school report cards](2026-01-30 The Gambia charts a path to data-driven education with DHIS2) are being built on a health-platform stack by the education ministry.
developments:
The build was documented on a study tour in May 2026 ([study tour](2026-05-04-gpe-kix-study-tour-education-data-system)) after the path was set out in January ([approach](2026-01-30 The Gambia charts a path to data-driven education with DHIS2)).

No coverage figure, school count or go-live date is published, so a national learner record is under construction with nothing yet measuring it.

summary: [Smart paper technology](2025-12-22 Smart Paper Technology is Transforming Community Health Data Capture in The Gambia) is in use for community health data capture, with no district count or record volume published.
developments:
It was documented in use in December 2025 ([capture](2025-12-22 Smart Paper Technology is Transforming Community Health Data Capture in The Gambia)).

It is the only health information system in the base, and a paper-based capture method digitised at the point of scanning is a different thing from a health management information system, which the country does not appear to hold.

summary: The police were [directed to move from paper to digital records](2026-03-24 Gambia Police must transition from paper documentation to digitalised mode - IGP) in March 2026, with no system, vendor, budget or timetable published.
developments:
The direction came from the Inspector General ([direction](2026-03-24 Gambia Police must transition from paper documentation to digitalised mode - IGP)).

Separately, mobile case-management applications and geographic facility mapping are in use under a donor-backed community policing programme, with no case volume published ([community policing](2026-03-23 From Essau to Gambisara - Reimagining Community Policing Across The Gambia)).

A directive with no procurement behind it and a donor programme with no volume behind it are the whole of the justice record.

summary: A [digital excise stamp](2026-07-30-gambia-digital-tax-stamp-sars-rwanda-study-visit) is in operation and studied by five foreign revenue administrations, on a claimed 95 per cent reduction in smuggling.
developments:
The claim carries no method and no independent verification, and every performance figure attached to the system is the collecting authority's own; the authority's earlier figures put excise collections at D48.47m for January to August 2024 against D6.31m in the same months of 2023 ([study visits](2026-07-30-gambia-digital-tax-stamp-sars-rwanda-study-visit)).

A digital tax invoicing system with tamper-proof signatures has been in service since July 2025 and is named in the ministry's reform account, still with no separate coverage or yield figure ([invoicing](2025-07-09 Gambia Gov't launches Digital Tax Invoicing System (GRA)), [reform account](2026-07-30-gambia-digital-reform-doubles-tax-revenue-d25b)).

An integrated tax administration system for electronic filing is named as planned, with no procurement, vendor, timetable or budget line published.

progress: Mixed, the financial management system has run unreported for years while a verification exercise was suspended mid-round
summary: The [financial management system](2016-09-27-wb-gmb-001-gambia-integrated-financial-management-information-system) has no statement of coverage or condition since 2020, and a staff verification round was [suspended in August 2026](2026-08-17-gambia-journal-gambia-halts-up-country-civil-servant).
developments:
The system is in service across ministries with revenue and treasury interfaces; the last date attached to it is a financing operation's closing year rather than a statement about the system ([financing](2016-09-27-wb-gmb-001-gambia-integrated-financial-management-information-system)).

The provincial round of a civil servant and pensioner verification exercise, scheduled for 17 to 23 August 2026, was suspended until further notice over unspecified technical difficulties, with the Greater Banjul round confirmed to start on 20 August; the difficulties are not described and no rescheduled date is given ([suspension](2026-08-17-gambia-journal-gambia-halts-up-country-civil-servant)).

2026-08-28 — the public service ministry told a ministerial interface that national identity card, passport and immigration procedures had been simplified and built into a digital services platform, which has not launched because of unresolved contractual issues over passport issuance, with rollout targeted before the end of 2026 starting with the machine-readable passport ([statement](2026-09-01-thepoint-gambia-id-card-passport-delays-mygov)). A platform complete and blocked on a contract is the same failure mode as the verification round suspended on unstated technical difficulties.

summary: A [digital innovation sprint](2026-07-09-young-gambians-digital-innovations-children-thepoint) was held in July 2026 with the youth council, the ministry and a United Nations agency.
developments:
No follow-on funding or incubation route is published ([sprint](2026-07-09-young-gambians-digital-innovations-children-thepoint)).

It is the only innovation event in the base, and a showcase without a route out of it is what the record shows.

summary: A [blockchain platform memorandum](2025-01-08-gambia-blockchain-pact-kalp-gambia-one-itweb) signed in January 2025 has produced no build, pilot, funding or withdrawal in nineteen months.
developments:
Nothing is on record being built under it ([memorandum](2025-01-08-gambia-blockchain-pact-kalp-gambia-one-itweb)).

No startup instrument, register, fund or incubator appears anywhere in the base, so a dormant memorandum is the entire startup record.

summary: A [domestically built payments platform](2026-07-20-gambia-accountant-general-sutura-digital-revenue-collection) was signed into government revenue collection in July 2026, distributed through the postal service.
developments:
No go-live date, volume, fee structure or list of connected banks is published, and no text of the memorandum is held ([memorandum](2026-07-20-gambia-accountant-general-sutura-digital-revenue-collection)).

It is the only domestically built system the base names in any sector, against an identity system produced with a foreign supplier, a data centre built with a foreign vendor and a mobile network to be modernised by a foreign investor.

summary: [400 women and girls were trained](2026-07-30-apc-gambia-rural-women-digital-rights) across four regions in eight workshops, with 40 community broadcasters and 80 peer mentors.
developments:
The programme ran between September 2025 and March 2026 and is funded by international impact grants with Swedish development support ([programme](2026-07-30-apc-gambia-rural-women-digital-rights)).

The implementer names unreliable internet, high data costs and unreliable electricity as the obstacles to continued practice, which is the base's only account of what stops a trained user from staying online.

summary: A [national labour digital skill programme](2025-12-23-validate-labour-digital-skill-report-thepoint) validated its methodology in December 2025 against a target of 280 certified.
developments:
It is funded at US$3.35m through the regional digital integration programme, and no completion figure has been published ([validation](2025-12-23-validate-labour-digital-skill-report-thepoint)).

A target of 280 certified is small against the country's labour force, and the base holds no other skills programme, certification count or employment outcome against which to place it.

summary: The [labour force survey published its fifth round](2026-07-30-gbos-glfs-2026-q1-findings-report) in July 2026 with the first systematic comparison across three rounds.
developments:
A sixth round is confirmed for later in 2026; both reports are donor-financed with international technical support, no domestic recurrent budget line for the series is established, and neither report's release date is published ([fifth round](2026-07-30-gbos-glfs-2026-q1-findings-report), [trend volume](2026-07-30-gbos-gambia-labour-market-progress-trends-2023-2026)).

Participation rose from 43.6 per cent in 2023 to 54.5 per cent in 2026, and unemployment fell from 7.6 per cent to 6.2 per cent, with labour underutilisation the wider measure at 23.6 and 32.1 per cent and no earlier round published for comparison ([trend volume](2026-07-30-gbos-gambia-labour-market-progress-trends-2023-2026)).

Agriculture's share of employment is given as 17.8 per cent, which the bureau states is a definitional change under a revised international standard excluding own-use food production rather than a movement out of farming ([findings](2026-07-30-standard-gm-gbos-labour-force-survey-2026-q1)).

summary: The central bank [convened producers and users of official statistics](2026-07-24-gambia-cbg-stakeholders-engagement-statistical-data) in July 2026, naming gaps, inconsistency and inaccessibility as the constraints.
developments:
The convening was with the International Monetary Fund and the statistics bureau, and no framework or workplan has been published ([convening](2026-07-24-gambia-cbg-stakeholders-engagement-statistical-data)).

It is the first convened coordination process on the record, and the three constraints it names are the same ones that make several figures on this ledger unverifiable: the authority's own tax numbers, the commission's own registration counts and the ministry's own attributions all lack an independent series to test them against.

summary: Cabinet approved a bill to establish a national research, development and innovation council ([approval](2026-08-29-linkedin-cabinet-approves-national-research-development-and-innovation-council)).
developments: Cabinet approved a bill to establish a national research, development and innovation council ([approval](2026-08-29-linkedin-cabinet-approves-national-research-development-and-innovation-council)). The council does not yet exist.

summary: The Gambia ranked third in sub-Saharan Africa on budget transparency in the 2025 open budget survey ([report](2026-08-27-foroyaa-gambia-open-budget-survey-2025-transparency)).
developments: The Gambia ranked third in sub-Saharan Africa on budget transparency in the 2025 open budget survey ([report](2026-08-27-foroyaa-gambia-open-budget-survey-2025-transparency)). Budget transparency is not the same as open data, and the base holds no dataset count.
